description: Unity UI Toolkit support boundary. Ordered; first match wins. Rules classify pointer families for the shapes the dispatcher admits (boolean form controls, select/toggle-item item groups, click-opened non-blocking anchored surfaces); whether a component is admitted at all is the dispatcher's decision, recorded per component in the capability inventory. `lowered` names what the emitter or shared C# runtime performs today; `pending` names the parity phase that will lower the family; `refused` states why UI Toolkit cannot realise the family idiomatically. Catch-all rules exist so that unknown prop families are never silently supported: an allowlisted component that reaches one fails generation until the family is adjudicated here.

phases.P2: Generic anatomy walker: ir.dom/ir.parts lower to a VisualElement tree; runtime bases become behaviors the generated constructor attaches.
phases.P3: Styling projection: generated USS from token facts, variants, states and box-model geometry; hand-authored palette removed.
phases.P4: Interaction families: static pressables, blocking and hover surfaces, composite and non-boolean form controls, month date grids, componentRef composition, messages, motion, typed C# declarations.
phases.P5: Corpus and admission: allowlist reaches the SwiftUI set; CI compile lane and committed-byte drift diff.

rules.reason: Authoring and validator metadata consumed by the contract validator; no target lowers it into runtime source.

rules.via: C# partial class name and the root USS class added in the generated constructor.

rules.reason: Documentation and classification metadata consumed by docs and audits; no target emits it into component source.
Agent-authoring metadata consumed by the a2ui runtime deriver, outside every emitter.
UI Toolkit panels are retained-mode and are never server-rendered or hydrated.
USS has no logical properties and no layout direction: the USS projection (uss.ts) lowers logical sides as LTR physical sides, so icon flipping and row reversal are not realised.

rules.via: uss.ts (S3): the box-model geometry profile reaches ir.nativeStyleRules as box-model.* slot definitions and structure consumers, which project into the generated Controls.uss.

rules.reason: The loading-text wrapper exists only to hold the pending-state chrome around the projected content. The native action lowering flattens the wrapper and makes the control's own contentContainer the projection point, so the wrapper is not rendered.

The spinner part is the guarded loading decoration of a DOM action control. Conditional componentRef composition is pending P4 and Spinner is not admitted to Unity, so the generated action control omits the part and exposes no loading state.

The guarded dismiss control is a native button or a composed Button carrying the dismissal callback; the passive lowering omits it and the boundary refuses its bindings, attributes and event. Composing the action control is the P4 composition family.
The dismiss part is guarded chrome omitted by the passive lowering, so its part identity is not rendered.
A guarded decoration whose content is a dynamic node prop has no static native projection. The passive lowering omits the decoration; the node-content prop stays pending P4.
The node-content decoration part is omitted by the passive lowering, so its part identity is not rendered.

rules.via: walker.ts (R2, R9): every declared part renders with part identity, name = <part>, the root class carrying cssPrefix and every other part <cssPrefix>__<part>; a parts-only contract synthesizes the tree from ir.parts in declared order.

rules.reason: Prose describing parts; documentation only.
Per-part ARIA roles and attributes have no runtime consumer: UI Toolkit exposes no assistive-technology tree.

rules.via: walker.ts (R1-R3): trigger parts and button tags lower to Button, text-leaf tags carrying content to Label, every other tag to VisualElement; the children tag and an unnamed slot are the contentContainer insertion point, a named slot a public <Name>Slot host.

walker.ts (R1, R4): each ir.compoundParts entry is its own [UxmlElement] <Name><Part> class the consumer composes; a part that opts out stays inline in its parent class. Composed content keeps document order: when a rendered sibling follows the first compound node, a private children host at that position is the contentContainer. Restrictions: an ItemGroup's trigger and content parts must stay compound, because the sub-element carries the IKeyedPart pairing key (opting out is refused with UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_INTERACTION); compound parts on both sides of a rendered sibling are pending P4 (refused with UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_ANATOMY until a second composed position exists).

walker.ts: the part renders with identity (R2); the root role is the generated class, and trigger and content roles are realised through the formControl, interaction and surface facts the IR validates against them (R1, R7).

rules.reason: Overlay parts belong to blocking surfaces and context parts are non-rendered providers; both arrive with the P4 blocking-surface and composition families.

Per-part focusability, interactivity and repetition are realised only where an attached behavior owns the part (trigger Buttons, item-group discovery of repeated compound parts); the walker sets no per-part focus or repetition itself.

A collapse intent replaces the anatomy with a native platform primitive; UI Toolkit's Toggle and Foldout own fixed internal trees the contract's anatomy does not describe, so the walker realises the declared anatomy instead.

rules.via: walker.ts: a componentRef node renders the admitted generated component class and carries its part identity on that instance.

rules.reason: Dynamic prop forwarding, event callbacks, guarded instance presence and nested instance content have no native component-ref lowering.

The loading decoration is a conditional componentRef to Spinner. Conditional componentRef composition is pending P4 and Spinner is not admitted to Unity, so the native action lowering omits the decoration instead of rendering an unadmitted reference.

rules.via: walker.ts instantiates the referenced generated class and forwards static prop attrs. References outside the target allowlist refuse generation.

walker.ts (R2): each part node inside a class is a public read-only element property named for the part, added to its parent in document order; an empty attribute or binding map declares nothing to lower.
walker.ts (R3): a named slot lowers to a public VisualElement <Name>Slot host at its position, named for the slot with class <cssPrefix>__<slot>.
The glyph anatomy plan validates the SVG presentation vocabulary; GlyphElement paints the authored catalog paths.

rules.reason: Static roles, ARIA attributes, element types and tab indices have no UI Toolkit consumer: there is no accessibility tree, the native Button owns activation, and focus order follows the element tree.
Other static attributes (SVG presentation, text-input hints, data attributes) are not lowered; an allowlisted component that declares one must be adjudicated here.

rules.via: The attached behavior's state class (R7): a binding to the selected channel's value on a trigger part is realised by BooleanControl, ItemGroup or AnchoredSurface toggling is-<value> on the host and, for item groups, on the paired parts. A binding to another channel or on a non-trigger part is unrealised and refuses generation.

walker.ts (R6): a disabled=prop:

binding on the form-control part names the prop emitted as the root's [UxmlAttribute] Disabled, mapped to SetEnabled.

rules.reason: Form serialization attributes (name, value) have no UI Toolkit counterpart: there is no form element to submit.
Dynamic roles and ARIA attributes have no runtime consumer: UI Toolkit exposes no assistive-technology tree.
A conditional DOM data attribute is not a UI Toolkit property. The passive walker checks its syntax and omits it; a target behavior must consume the prop before the attribute can affect rendering.
The root's type binding selects native form submission; UI Toolkit has no form element to serialise into, so the native action root does not lower it.

DOM element properties (for example a checkbox's indeterminate flag) have no UI Toolkit consumer: BooleanControl realises the checked channel and SetEnabled only, and the generated control exposes no DOM property.
Other attribute and DOM-property bindings need typed C# props; an allowlisted component that declares one must be adjudicated here.

rules.via: The generated root derives from UnityEngine.UIElements.Button; its native clicked event (pointer activation and Space/Enter submit alike) invokes the generated callback property named from this binding.

rules.reason: Authored DOM event handlers need P4 callback declarations. The form-control change event and trigger activation are synthesized by the IR and realised by the attached behavior, not authored here.

Prop, message, projection and transform content needs typed C# props and the message catalog; the walker renders the element (a Label for text leaves) without text. Only literal content lowers (Label.text / Button.text, R5).

Prop and slot presence guards are not lowered: the walker refuses a guarded node (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_ANATOMY) rather than render it unconditionally. The presence guard the IR synthesizes on an unmount content part is realised by the attached behavior.
Repeated rendering is not lowered; the walker refuses an iterated node (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_ANATOMY).
Prop-driven CSS custom properties need generated USS variables and typed props; the walker emits nothing for them.

rules.via: The glyph anatomy plan binds name and size hints to GlyphElement; its generated catalog paints the authored paths.

walker.ts (R2, R3): slot anchors are the walker's part identity (UQuery by name or <cssPrefix>__<part> class replaces the DOM data-slot selector) and named-slot hosts; required is a composition obligation the usage audit checks, not a runtime fact.
[UxmlAttribute] value property (Checked, Open, Value with Values) on the generated root, delegating to the attached behavior; SetValueWithoutNotify silently updates boolean channels.
Imperative initial assignment: a value assigned before panel attachment is the uncontrolled initial state; no separate default property is emitted.
RegisterValueChangedCallback for boolean channels and the ValueChanged C# event for selection channels; Controlled + ValueRequested realise the owner-controlled half of the trio.

rules.reason: HTML form submission fields (name, value) have no UI Toolkit counterpart: there is no form element to serialise into.

rules.via: [UxmlAttribute] Disabled mapped to SetEnabled on the control root; disabled activation leaves state unchanged.

rules.reason: The DOM button type selects native form submission; UI Toolkit has no form element to serialise into, so the generated action control exposes no Type property.
The pending state renders through a conditional Spinner decoration (pending P4, Spinner unadmitted). The generated action control exposes no Loading property and omits the decoration.
ARIA state attributes have no UI Toolkit consumer: the runtime exposes no assistive-technology tree.

rules.via: The generated action root exposes a public Action property named from this callback prop; the native Button.clicked event invokes it (pointer activation and Space/Enter submit alike).

walker.ts item-group vocabulary (R6): [UxmlAttribute] Type, Orientation and ActivationMode (validated against their variant axes) and Collapsible, Loop and UnmountInactive on the generated root drive the attached ItemGroup's SelectionType, Orientation, ActivationMode, Collapsible, Loop and UnmountInactive; emitted only when the contract declares the prop and ItemGroup is attached, initialised from the declared default.

walker.ts item-group vocabulary (R6): [UxmlAttribute] Appearance validated against its variant axis toggles the root's class-recipe modifier (<cssPrefix>--<value>), which the generated USS keys (uss.ts).

[UxmlAttribute] CloseOnEscape / CloseOnOutsideClick / CloseOnBlur on the generated root drive the attached AnchoredSurface's CloseOn<Event> knobs, initialised from the trigger's defaultEnabled; only modes the surface declares start enabled.
[UxmlAttribute] Placement on the generated root, validated against its variant axis, drives the attached AnchoredSurface; floating content flips and shifts at panel edges.

rules.reason: The list-marker axis projects only to CSS list-style-type, which USS does not implement; the generated control exposes no Marker property and the marker declarations stay ledgered.

List spacing selects sibling children with child-combinator rules the native selector grammar refuses, so the projection carries no spacing rules and the generated control withholds Spacing until P4 lowers that selector family.

rules.via: The generated [UxmlAttribute] property validates the authored axis and switches the root modifier class. Admission checks that the corresponding USS carrier exists.

rules.reason: A UI Toolkit control cannot change its underlying semantic element tag; the native type is fixed by the generated class.
Text alignment, case transformation and measured ellipsis need a native TextElement consumer. The current class has no corresponding attribute or style behavior.
An authored rule-thickness override needs a validated native length and orientation-aware border update; token-backed default thickness is separate.

rules.via: The normalized iconGlyph.nameFrom prop becomes a generated UXML property that drives GlyphElement catalog lookup.

rules.reason: UI Toolkit exposes no assistive-technology tree for the icon's ARIA label.
Decorative role and title describe DOM accessibility/tooltip semantics without an equivalent UI Toolkit runtime consumer on the supported desktop witness.

These contracts declare a size variant axis but their styles sidecars carry no size-predicated rules, so the USS projection has no class carrier and the generated control withholds Size. Adding size style rules lowers the axis without an emitter change.
The web indeterminate (mixed) checkbox state has no BooleanControl realisation: the shared behavior carries one boolean channel, so the generated control exposes no Indeterminate property.
ARIA labelling and description relationships have no UI Toolkit consumer: the runtime exposes no assistive-technology tree, so the generated control does not emit these props.

rules.via: walker.ts (S6) emits [UxmlAttribute] Size as the class-recipe modifier (<cssPrefix>--<value>) only when the USS projection emits a carrier for the axis; uss.ts lowers size-predicated native style rules onto those carriers.

rules.reason: DOM id generation exists to wire ARIA relationships; UI Toolkit has no id-referenced accessibility relationships.
DOM attribute passthrough; UI Toolkit controls expose typed properties, not arbitrary host attributes.
The citation URL is a document-link semantic (HTML cite) with no UI Toolkit consumer; the generated container exposes no Cite property.
Structured object props need typed C# declaration lowering and a native content composer; the generated container exposes no Profile property until that P4 family lands.
Dynamic node content needs a typed C# content projection (P4). The generated passive container exposes no Icon property and omits the guarded decoration.
Dismissal is action chrome on a guarded child the passive lowering omits; the flag, callback and label are refused rather than exposed as an inert API, and composing the action control is P4.
The status-icon flag only selects the omitted node-content icon decoration; the generated container exposes no ShowStatusIcon property.
Prop families not yet adjudicated for UI Toolkit. An allowlisted component may not rely on this rule: add a family rule above.

rules.via: The one channel the dispatcher selects maps its value/default/change trio to the C# value property, pre-attachment assignment and change callback or event; Controlled + ValueRequested carry owner-controlled state. A second channel is unrealised and refuses generation.

rules.reason: Named types lower to C# string/bool today; enums, unions and records need typed C# declarations.

rules.via: uss.ts (S4): a variant predicate lowers to the class-recipe modifier carrier .<cssPrefix>--<value> on the root or as the part's ancestor; the walker emits the axis as a [UxmlAttribute] when a behavior knob consumes it or a carrier exists. A modifier with no Unity carrier is listed uss-selector in Controls.unsupported.json.

uss.ts (S4): a state predicate lowers to the behavior's state class at its placement (host for BooleanControl and AnchoredSurface, paired parts for ItemGroup), to native :hover/:active/:focus/:disabled, or to BooleanControl's mirrored is-hover/is-active/is-focus host classes; what USS cannot select is listed in Controls.unsupported.json (uss-pseudo, uss-owner-mismatch, uss-floating-scope).

rules.reason: USS has no @keyframes; it supports property transitions only. Keyframe animation would need a scheduler-driven C# runtime, which is not an idiomatic lowering of a stylesheet fact.
USS transitions, loops and reduced-motion gating are not generated yet.

rules.via: Events emitted through the selected channel's change prop surface as RegisterValueChangedCallback (boolean) or the ValueChanged C# event (selection); C# signatures use arrays for both selection modes. Any other event is unrealised and refuses generation.

rules.reason: Transitions are implemented by hand in ItemGroup and AnchoredSurface; there is no generic state-machine lowering.
No HTML form participation, constraint validation or field association exists in UI Toolkit.

rules.via: The dispatcher attaches the BooleanControl behavior for boolean value models (R7).
The form-control part renders as the Button BooleanControl.Attach binds (exposed as Trigger); the channel selects the generated C# value property and constants.
BooleanControl commits on trigger activation, which is the change moment of a boolean control; there is no intermediate input phase to defer.
BooleanControl.Attach binds the control's native Button.clicked event, which is the activation commit the contract declares; no separate change event is emitted.

rules.reason: Non-boolean value models and commit policies need their own runtime behavior and an explicit decision here.
Composite controls (Select, RadioGroup, …) need a composite runtime behavior; the dispatcher rejects them today.
A month date grid (Calendar) needs a date-grid runtime behavior: locale-formatted weeks, roving focus over gridcells and the value and month channels; the dispatcher rejects it today.

A dual-listbox transfer (Shuttle) needs a transfer-list runtime behavior: the available and selected lists derived from the options prop and the value channel, a mark per item, add and remove, and per-list focus; its iterated options are refused with the rest of anatomy iteration.

rules.via: The dispatcher attaches ItemGroup for select / toggle-item and AnchoredSurface for toggle; ItemGroup.Attach(…, operation, …) carries the operation into the runtime.

The trigger and content parts are generated keyed sub-elements (R4) the attached behavior discovers under the host by <cssPrefix>__<part> class; the channel selects the generated value property and constants.
The named prop is emitted as [UxmlAttribute] Disabled and gates activation through SetEnabled.

The dispatcher admits hidden only on ItemGroup (inactive content hidden, detached when UnmountInactive is set) and unmount only on AnchoredSurface (floating content removed on close); other pairings are refused.

rules.reason: Other operations (open, close, …), multi-trigger interactions and remaining interaction facts have no runtime behavior and need an explicit decision here.

rules.via: ItemGroup.Attach(…, orientation, wrap) initialises arrow-key orientation and wrapping; declared orientation / loop props override them through the item-group vocabulary.

The dispatcher pairs each strategy with the behavior that realises it and refuses other pairings (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_FOCUS): roving and manual on ItemGroup (passed to Attach; arrow / Home / End navigation), auto on BooleanControl (native Button focus), none on AnchoredSurface (no trap; focus stays on the trigger or moves into the content).

rules.reason: The initial focus target is not read. ItemGroup's roving tabIndex makes the active tab, or every trigger, the first tab stop regardless of the declared part; a declared target that differs would be ignored.
Prose description of the focus strategy; documentation only.
Focus trapping, restoration and other focus facts are not lowered and need an explicit decision here.

rules.via: AnchoredSurface reparents floating content to the panel root and re-attaches the stylesheet; the dispatcher refuses any non-surface shape that enables a portal (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_PORTAL).
Content stays in the document tree; the dispatcher refuses an anchored surface whose portal is disabled because AnchoredSurface always reparents (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_SURFACE).
The panel root is the UI Toolkit equivalent of document.body.
AnchoredSurface.Reposition anchors to the trigger's world bound and flips/shifts at panel edges.

rules.reason: USS has no z-index: UI Toolkit orders siblings by hierarchy and AnchoredSurface brings floating content to the front of the panel root, so named layers have no USS realisation.
Other portal targets, positioning or collision policies need an explicit decision here.

rules.via: AnchoredSurface CloseOnEscape / CloseOnOutsideClick / CloseOnBlur over the anchor/content union.
The named prop is emitted as the matching [UxmlAttribute] CloseOn* flag.
An empty trigger list declares no dismissal; the attached behaviors register none.

rules.reason: pointer-leave, close-button and other dismissal triggers need the blocking and hover surface behaviors and an explicit decision here.

rules.via: The dispatcher attaches AnchoredSurface for non-blocking surfaces.
The trigger Button's clicked event toggles the surface.
The anchor and content parts are generated sub-elements (R1, R4) AnchoredSurface.Attach discovers under the host by <cssPrefix>__<part> class.

Interactive surface content is a generated ScrollView sub-element (R1) the behavior makes focusable; the dispatcher refuses non-interactive content because the runtime cannot make it inert (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_SURFACE).

rules.reason: aria-controls / aria-expanded relations have no assistive-technology consumer in UI Toolkit.

rules.via: The dispatcher admits part-anchored popovers only; AnchoredSurface.Reposition anchors to the trigger and flips/shifts at panel edges.
The named prop is emitted as [UxmlAttribute] Placement and drives Reposition.
The Content object is retained while closed (detached from the hierarchy, not disposed); the dispatcher refuses other presence values (UNITY_UNSUPPORTED_SURFACE).

rules.reason: Blocking modality, hover/focus open triggers and remaining surface facts need the blocking and hover surface behaviors and an explicit decision here.
Id-referenced ARIA relationships; UI Toolkit exposes no assistive-technology tree that could consume them.

rules.via: ItemGroup arrow / Home / End navigation and native Button submit activation (Space / Enter) through NavigationSubmitEvent.

rules.reason: Roles, labels and ARIA attributes have no runtime consumer: UI Toolkit exposes no assistive-technology tree on desktop, and Unity's mobile AccessibilityHierarchy is not populated by UI Toolkit. Revisit when that integration exists.
The component message catalog is not lowered for Unity; generated controls carry no localisable text.
Truncation policy needs USS text-overflow projection and a measuring runtime.
Sequence and paged-set position policies need their own runtime behavior.
UI Toolkit has no CSS grid layout; uss.ts lists a grid display declaration as uss-scalar instead of treating it as a flexbox equivalent.
USS has no grid-template-rows or animated grid track sizing; uss.ts lists the declaration as uss-property.

The USS property table (uss.ts) has no lowering for these CSS properties: USS (Unity 6000.5) has no box-shadow, line-height, keyframe animation, contain, clip or CSS text-transform; draw order is visual-tree order, not z-index; picking is VisualElement.pickingMode, set from C#, not pointer-events; -unity-text-align couples both axes where CSS text-align controls only the horizontal axis; a CSS font-family list has no source-bound native font asset. Each declaration is listed uss-property in Controls.unsupported.json.

uss.ts maps no CSS cursor keyword: a runtime USS cursor is a texture with a hotspot, which the contract does not carry (USS's named cursors apply in the Editor only). Each declaration is listed uss-scalar.
uss.ts paints a focus outline as the element's own border, which cannot stand off the box; only a zero offset is realised. Each other offset is listed uss-property.

-unity-font-style carries bold and normal only; an intermediate weight (100-300, 500) needs a font asset per weight, which the token graph does not carry. Classified by the declared value; uss.ts decides a token-fed weight by the token's value in every theme and brand scope, and Controls.unsupported.json records that outcome (uss-scalar, or uss-var-composite when the scopes disagree).

A USS transition names USS properties and a keyword easing: a transition of transform (USS splits it into translate, rotate and scale) or with a cubic-bezier, steps or token-fed easing does not carry its CSS meaning. uss.ts keeps the realisable parts (properties, durations, ease) and lists the rest under the transition's longhand in Controls.unsupported.json.
USS lengths are px or % literals; calc() has no USS form and uss.ts does not evaluate it. Each declaration is listed uss-scalar.
An em length depends on the computed font size of its parent; the fixed-root rem conversion cannot preserve that relative value. The USS projection lists it uss-scalar.
USS does not accept currentColor as a color scalar. The glyph renderer inherits its host's resolved foreground instead; uss.ts records the authored declaration as uss-scalar.

A component slot is defined only with one USS scalar (length, percentage, number, time, angle, colour, keyword, a rem value resolved against the fixed 16px native root, or a var() with a scalar fallback). A multi-component value (shadow list, two-value padding, font-family list), an easing function or an unresolved relative unit (em, ch, vw, vh) has no USS custom-property form uss.ts emits; each definition is listed uss-scalar.
The dismissal style selectors target the omitted guarded chrome; P4 composition re-enables the action control and its state styles.

The IR's native style grammar refuses the selector key (an attribute or ARIA state such as [aria-expanded], a web-template state class such as <part>--active, a combinator, or a structural pseudo-class), so no native style rule exists for USS to lower and uss.ts lists the key uss-selector. The IR-facts spec that carries these states as contract state predicates precedes P4, which lowers them.

rules.via: uss.ts (S2/S3): token bindings become component custom properties var(--fsds-<graph path>, <fallback>) over a generated token section (.fsds-theme light, .fsds-theme--dark, .fsds-brand-<id>) projected from resolved.tokens.json and the token build's @layer brand.

rules.reason: The USS projection has no transition-duration/transition-timing-function or font-style handler and USS has no user-select, list-style-type or list-style property; the projection lists each such declaration uss-property in Controls.unsupported.json.
USS has no intrinsic sizing keywords; the projection lists these declarations uss-scalar in Controls.unsupported.json.
USS has no pseudo-elements; the projection lists every declaration of such a selector key uss-pseudo-element.
The web indeterminate (mixed) pseudo-class has no Unity state; the projection lists its declarations uss-pseudo.

rules.via: uss.ts (S3-S5): each native style rule becomes one USS rule through the CSS-to-USS property table (gap lowers to --fsds-gap, realised by the runtime Gap helper; a composed-content host restates its owner's container declarations); a declaration USS cannot realise is listed with its reason in Controls.unsupported.json, generated beside Controls.uss.
